prompt: Let A={u,v}, B={p,q,r}, C={0,1}. Let g:A→B and f:B→C be functions, and suppose f∘g:A→C is surjective. Determine which of the following properties are logically forced: (i) f is surjective; (ii) g is surjective; (iii) f is injective. Prove every forced property and give a fully specified countermodel for each property that is not forced.

Find every integer x satisfying x ≡ 4 (mod 9), x ≡ 7 (mod 10), and x ≡ 3 (mod 11). Determine the unique solution class modulo 990. Give a derivation using the Chinese remainder theorem or an equivalent method, then verify the result independently in all three congruences. Explain why the solution is unique modulo 990.

Using RFC 3986 §2.1 and §6.2.2.2, assess the following URI components: %7Ealice, ~alice, %2F, and /. Explain (a) whether hexadecimal letter case in percent-encoding matters, (b) when a percent-encoded octet may be decoded during normalization, and (c) whether %2F may generally be normalized to / without changing the reserved-character semantics. Cite the relevant RFC sections and distinguish a standards rule from an implementation-specific assumption.

Two hospitals report outcomes for treatments A and B. In Hospital 1, A has 9 successes among 10 patients and B has 80 successes among 100 patients. In Hospital 2, A has 1 success among 100 patients and B has 0 successes among 10 patients. (1) Compute each treatment's success rate within each hospital. (2) Compute each treatment's pooled success rate across both hospitals. (3) Explain how the within-hospital comparisons and pooled comparison can point in opposite directions. (4) State precisely what these descriptive data do and do not establish about a causal treatment effect.

Consider the claim: “For every nonempty finite list of real numbers with arithmetic mean m, at least one entry in the list is equal to m.” Determine whether the claim is true. If it is false, give a counterexample with the smallest possible list length, prove that no shorter counterexample exists, and state a correct general property relating the mean to the entries.
